anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after staged transcode envelope routing, clip filtering, tuple preparation, transit and shadow context assembly, whose own body constructs the target observable typed-array payload value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging a return value, or emitting to console.

primary_anchor.source_export: private helper reached through exported u(config)
primary_anchor.why: First target-specific value-construction function: it normalizes the media tuple into source text, materializes the target Uint8Array through its helpers, and returns the observable ta_ typed_array_payload string.
primary_anchor.answer_basis: Agent-visible corpus only: the canonical anchor answer is captured_span plus answer_function as declared in the captured bundle slice. The bundle is obfuscated (hexadecimal identifier names), so answer_function is the mangled _0x name an agent actually sees; source_function is a private maintainer mapping into src/.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span in the captured bundle (hash/offset/complete function body). Agents only see captures, so the standard answer identifier is primary_anchor.answer_function (the mangled bundle name), not source_function.
A returned function name is scored against answer_function in the captured corpus. source_function is a private maintainer label that an agent cannot know because the bundle mangles every identifier.

Agent explanation distinguishes the anchor from staged transcode session handlers, envelope routers, clip filters, routing, input preparation, tuple normalization, byte materialization, encoding helper, wrapper, sink and off-chain decoy functions.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function in the captured corpus.

role_oracle.why: First target-specific value-construction function: it normalizes the media tuple into source text, materializes the target Uint8Array through its helpers, and returns the observable ta_ typed_array_payload string.
Materializes the 18-byte Uint8Array that carries the transformed media tuple lanes, transit values and shadow-sensitive context consumed by the payload encoder.
Serializes the transformed Uint8Array into the ta_ base64url typed_array_payload string observed in the console object.
Computes the per-lane 32-bit words that feed the target Uint8Array materialization helper.

Builds the canonical media tuple source string (ordered fields, transit, shadow and mid context) that the anchor digests; a direct target-specific callee alongside materializeMediaBytes and encodeTypedArrayPayload, not a reusable generic utility.
Generic tuple-to-map conversion utility used before source-text and byte-array construction.
Generic media-tuple normalizer/sorter that orders the rows before canonical source construction; not target-specific.
Exported factory that closes over the slot config and returns the per-slot reducer that calls the anchor; it does not itself materialize the Uint8Array or encode the payload.
Returned transformer closure that delegates to transformMediaTypedArray without constructing the payload itself.
Selects the live slot-29 converter instance and invokes it on the prepared media tuple, transit and shadow context.
Routes the transcode.buffer.commit branch into tuple preparation, converter production and the console payload wrapper.
Builds the slot-29 media config descriptor (slot, batch, salt, lane) consumed by the converter selection.
Chooses the slot-29 media config used by the live converter instance.
Console sink that freezes the already constructed payload, paints it, and logs it with console.log; it should not outrank the constructor anchor.
Packages the already constructed typed_array_payload value into the console payload object with the transcode.buffer.commit metadata; it does not construct the value.
Paints the typed_array_payload into the transcode status panel but does not construct it.
Reconstructs the typed_array_payload field name at the sink from a character-code array; builds the observable key, not the payload value.
Reconstructs the transcode.buffer.commit action label at the sink from a character-code array; builds the observable label, not the payload value.
Emits media.shadow.action diversion output over the shadow function pool and is explicitly outside the requested transcode.buffer.commit typed_array_payload target.

scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span

do_not_promote: The final console sink and payload wrappers emit an already encoded typed_array_payload value.
The exported factory only wraps the private typed-array anchor and should not outrank the anchor itself.

Staged transcode routing (session control, envelope routing, clip collection, tuple preparation), config selection, painting and dynamic sink field reconstruction are path-critical preparation or output wrappers, not the target value constructor.
The shadow transcode trace path can emit debug objects during interaction but does not carry typed_array_payload under transcode.buffer.commit.
The target value is deterministic for the same codec profile, render mode, frame budget, operator tag and sync strict settings and sensitive to changes in those controls.
debug_hints_private: The primary anchor is visible in the captured bundle as an obfuscated _0x function whose body calls createSource, materializeMediaBytes and encodeTypedArrayPayload.
The target field name typed_array_payload is reassembled at the sink from a character-code array.
The byte materialization helper contains new Uint8Array(18).
The page path uses prime, pack and commit staged buttons with codec profile, render mode, frame budget, operator tag and sync strict controls before commit routes into the transformation chain.
Source paths are private evaluator mapping aids, not the default public answer space; the bundle mangles every identifier so source names are not searchable in captures.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Returned span maps uniquely to the captured transformMediaTypedArray anchor function (createSource + materializeMediaBytes + encodeTypedArrayPayload).
Returned span maps to a target-specific helper that the anchor digests, such as createSource, materializeMediaBytes, encodeTypedArrayPayload or laneWord.
Returned span maps to a generic core utility directly used by the typed-array transformation path, such as makePlainMap.
Returned span maps to a path-critical routing, config-selection or paint function, the factory wrapper, or a payload/sink wrapper that only emits an already constructed value.

Returned span maps to a generic path helper that normalizes/orders tuple inputs or reconstructs an observable field name or action label from a character-code array, such as normalizeTuple, targetField or actionValue.
Returned span maps to an off-chain shadow decoy or cannot be uniquely mapped to a captured function.
